label: Original-phase steps t>=2 and <DEL> in sequences whose first token is h/f/1/e/j/z/x/u
explanation: Fires almost only during input reading: original-phase steps from t=2 onward plus the <DEL> step (98% of mass; it is essentially silent in the copy phase, at t=0, and weak at t=1). Rates peak at t=2-3 and fall off with position. Which sequences it fires in depends mostly on the first original token: h is strongest (4x lift, 30% of mass), then f, 1, e, then j, z, x, u. The top activations are sequences beginning h h ... with the peak at <DEL> or at a new token (a, w, s, m, p) right after the h run. Fires mostly on first occurrences of a token (93% of mass), and current input a raises the rate (3.7x). Repeated h inputs themselves get only weak activation. There is also a long tail of weak activations at t>=2 in sequences that start with other tokens, which is what limits precision and recall.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: h, 1, f, e, j, z; least: l, t, w, a) and the current input token, by step (t=0: a; t=1: a, w, s, m; t=2: a, w, s, m); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=3 & t=5.
